summary: Obfuscated self-updating remote-control agent daemon with PTY/SSH/Python exec surface
details: @whalent/agent-core@0.3.289 ships as a Node.js daemon whose primary executable dist/index.cjs is a 14 MB bundle packed with obfuscator.io transforms (rotated string array a0_0x3e75, hex-named identifiers, decoder function a0_0x2334). All network destinations are reconstructed at runtime from the obfuscated string array; no plaintext http(s) URLs are visible in the bundle. The package's own README describes the daemon as remote-upgradable ("the package replaced by remote daemon upgrades"), and the dependency graph includes ssh2 and optional node-pty. A bundled Python sidecar (jupyter_sidecar.py) reads NDJSON from stdin and executes arbitrary code strings via a Jupyter client: `client.execute(code,...)` where `code` comes from `params.get("code", "")`. Together these give a remote party a self-replacing update path plus PTY, SSH, and Python execution primitives on the host that runs the daemon, with the control channel opaque to static inspection due to the obfuscation. Obfuscation of a server-side Node daemon (not a browser bundle) defeats installer-side auditing of where the agent connects and what commands it will accept.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
